messages:
maria_support: FYI — customer 'ACME Corp' opened a billing escalation: they were billed ~480 reserved GPU hours for March but their token/throughput dashboards only show ~120 GPU-equivalent hours. Case CS-2026-139. Can someone triage the meter vs billing pipeline?

kenji_engineering: can you paste the org_id and the dedicated pool id? also any CSV export or invoice line items would help.

maria_support: org_id=org_acme_9, pool=dgd-us-west-1-poolA. Attached CSV (exported from billing UI):
```
invoice_line,amount,period
reserved_capacity_hours,480,2026-03
burst_hours_credit,0,2026-03
usage_tokens,1.2M,2026-03
```
Dashboard 'Reserved Capacity > utilization' shows steady 20-25% GPU utilization.

jonathan_infra: quick checks: has the billing ingestion job (billing-ingest-v2) been restarted or replayed in March? replay could double-count. infra-bot, did we have any replays?

infra-bot: billing-ingest-v2 job restart events: 2026-03-05T03:12:21Z (manual restart by deploy bot), 2026-03-10T11:44:02Z (crash + auto-retry). No explicit replay flagged.

kenji_engineering: ok. another common mismatch is GPU-hours measured in scheduler_time vs billable_time. Scheduler can over-allocate (pre-warm) and then free w/o token traffic but still count as reserved hours. Can you pull allocator metrics for poolA for March 1-15?

maria_support: pasted allocator snippet from internal dashboard (aggregated):
```
metric,gpu_seconds
allocator_allocated_seconds,1728000  # ~480 GPU hours
allocator_active_seconds,432000     # ~120 GPU hours
```
This looks like allocated != active.

kenji_engineering: that helps. If allocated_seconds is being treated as the billable unit (we expect active_seconds), that'll cause the delta. I'll check mapping in the billing transform (repo: billing/transform/usage_mapper.py).

kenji_engineering: quick grep: `grep -n "allocated_seconds" billing/transform/usage_mapper.py` returns a block where allocated_seconds is used when active_seconds is null. If allocator started emitting allocated_seconds for a period (we changed allocator behavior on 2026-03-01 behind a flag), that could explain it.

oli_billing: linking invoice line items: our billing pipeline intentionally bills 'reserved_capacity_hours' based on the ingestion metric named `gpu_hours_consumed` which historically was mapped to allocator_allocated_seconds/3600. We recently intended to switch to allocator_active_seconds for customers on Dedicated but the migration was only half-rolled. Looks like org_acme_9 was on the old mapping.

maria_support: customer says they did not use burst. they confirmed no heavy token requests in March and are upset.

jonathan_infra: root cause hypothesis: a config flag flip on 2026-03-01 toggled the allocator to emit allocated_seconds for poolA; billing transform still using allocated_seconds for some orgs. Also there were billing-ingest restarts (3/05 and 3/10) but infra-bot shows no replay, so likely data consistent but wrong metric selection.

kenji_engineering: reproduction steps to confirm: run the local mapper on org_acme_9's raw usage blob for March and compare outputs:
```
# fetch raw blob
aws s3 cp s3://usage-raw/2026/03/org_acme_9/usage-blob-2026-03-01.json .
python billing/transform/usage_mapper.py --input usage-blob-2026-03-01.json --prefer active_seconds > mapped-output.json
jq '.billable_hours' mapped-output.json
```

maria_support: I've requested the raw blob and shared it in the case.

oli_billing: remediation plan: 1) run reconciliation for March for org_acme_9 and all pools that had allocator behavior change; 2) if we confirm overbill, issue provisional credit equal to delta and mark invoice for adjustment; 3) patch usage_mapper to prefer active_seconds for Dedicated pools and roll forward a backfill job for March ingestion.

jonathan_infra: small caution: when we backfill, we must ensure idempotency; the ingestion IDs used for dedupe were changed on 2026-02-28. I'll double-check dedupe keys. If keys mismatch, backfill could create duplicates.

kenji_engineering: I'll open a PR to change default mapping and add a safety check to reject allocated_seconds-based billing for Dedicated customer tiers. Also add a test with the sample blob.

maria_support: customer asked for ETA on credit. We should give provisional timeline.

oli_billing: provisional: run local mapping today, run reconciliation tomorrow morning, if delta confirmed we can issue provisional credit same day (manual billing adjustment). Final audit for formal invoice adjustment by end of week. I'll file a billing ticket. Ticket: BILL-2026-884.

kenji_engineering: noted. Action items: kenji -> PR and tests; jonathan -> verify dedupe keys for backfill; oli -> create billing ticket and provisional credit workflow; maria -> keep customer updated with case CS-2026-139.

maria_support: customer updated: they appreciate fast answers, want a short explanation and compensation. I'll propose a brief note: 'We discovered a metric mapping bug that caused allocated (pre-warm) GPU time to be billed; we're reconciling and issuing credit.' ok?

oli_billing: that's fine. Please avoid technical jargon in customer note. Close loop with legal before sending if amount > $10k.

maria_support: thanks, will do. tagging this thread to track until billing ticket resolved.

jonathan_infra: FYI after PR + backfill we should add an alert for delta between allocated_seconds and active_seconds > 2x for any pool — that would catch regressions.

kenji_engineering: agreed, will add alert to eng-platform playbook.

maria_support: closing note to internal thread: next update after reconciliation run tomorrow. "
